problem.concept: It is not clear if emotions in e-communities primarily derive from individual group members' personalities or if they result from intra-group interactions, and whether they influence group activities.

task.concept: Could emotions in Internet exchanges affect others and systematically influence quantitative and qualitative aspects of the trajectory of e-communities?

method.concept: posts were grouped into clusters of messages with similar emotional valences

contribution.concept: 4 million posts downloaded from Blogs, Digg and BBC forums: posts were grouped into clusters of messages with similar emotional valences. The frequency of long clusters was much higher than it would be if emotions occurred at random.

clusters of messages with similar emotional valences: Distributions for cluster lengths can be explained by preferential processes because conditional probabilities for consecutive messages grow as a power law with cluster length.

For BBC forum threads, average discussion lengths were higher for larger values of absolute average emotional valence in the first ten comments and the average amount of emotion in messages fell during discussions.

4 million posts downloaded from Blogs, Digg and BBC forums: collective emotional states can be created and modulated via Internet communication and that emotional expressiveness is the fuel that sustains some e-communities.

problem.concept: whether supervision with hierarchical structure enhances learning of a range of grammatical dependencies, a question that has previously been addressed only for subject-verb agreement.

method.concept: incrementalized version of the Parsing-as-Language-Modeling configuration

contribution.concept: Negative Polarity licensing and Filler--Gap Dependencies. Using the same training data across models, we find that structurally-supervised models outperform the LSTM, with the RNNG demonstrating best results on both types of grammatical dependencies and even learning many of the Island Constraints on the filler--gap dependency.

Models are tested on a diverse range of configurations for two classes of non-local grammatical dependencies in English---Negative Polarity licensing and Filler--Gap Dependencies. Structural supervision thus provides data efficiency advantages over purely string-based training of neural language models in acquiring human-like generalizations about non-local grammatical dependencies.

problem.concept: most existing approaches rely on supervised machine learning (ML) and substantial labeled data that are expensive to develop and apply to different sub-fields of biomedicine.

task.concept: information structure analysis of full scientific articles

contribution.concept: novel corpus of 50 biomedical articles annotated according to the Argumentative Zoning (AZ) scheme
two novel applications that use AZ to support real-life literature review in biomedicine via question answering and summarization

50 biomedical articles annotated according to the Argumentative Zoning (AZ) scheme: active learning with SVM trained on 500 labeled sentences (6% of the corpus) performs surprisingly well with the accuracy of 82%, just 2% lower than fully supervised learning.
In our question answering task, biomedical researchers find relevant information significantly faster from AZ-annotated than unannotated articles.
In the summarization task, sentences extracted from particular zones are significantly more similar to gold standard summaries than those extracted from particular sections of full articles.
